CBC and platelets are normal, PT and thrombin time are essentially normal, with an isolated prolongation of the intrinsic pathway test (ACT reported prolonged — consistent with an elevated aPTT). A family history of a maternal uncle with similar problems points to an X-linked inheritance. The constellation (male child, spontaneous hemarthrosis, isolated intrinsic pathway prolongation, X-linked family history) is most consistent with hemophilia. Hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) is far more common than hemophilia B, so the single most likely diagnosis is hemophilia A; confirmatory testing should include factor VIII activity level and genetic testing, and management requires hematology referral and factor replacement as indicated. 

DIAGNOSIS: Hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency)
